evidence.claims: Checked README and whitepaper numbers against results.txt: 0.0326 vs 0.0331, 3.9x/33x/165x, h=4/18, error <=2.4e-7, 2.0-4.5x slower, 0.033->0.070-0.088, P(miss) 0.38/0.42/0.33/0.30/0.14, '6 tests', '~3 s' (1.7 s) all backed. Slips: 'doubles the error' is 2.2-2.7x (README:3, page); 'cuts that to <= 4%' but n=50 gives 0.0402 (README:3, page); alpha^theta '2-3x off' is 1.7-3.3x on the quoted row (whitepaper:13, README:15). Novelty framing ('the contribution is the exact real-human consequences', whitepaper:19) does not say these are Wald's OC and ASN functions evaluated off-design. README and whitepaper carry no AI-assistance note; the served page does.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: Wald (1945, 1947 Sequential Analysis) operating-characteristic L(p) and average-sample-number functions of the binomial SPRT, which for the symmetric walk are exactly results 1-3 (cited as 'the method', not as the result); gambler's ruin (Feller, cited). HRI: Fisac et al. RSS 2018 'Probabilistically safe robot planning with confidence-based human predictions' infers the human's rationality online jointly with prediction, which is this paper's 'next step'; Milli & Dragan UAI 2019 and Bobu et al. HRI 2020 on human-model misspecification; Reddy, Dragan & Levine NeurIPS 2018. None of the HRI misspecification work is cited and no baseline (e.g. Bayesian/LCB online estimation of p, a mixture-over-p likelihood) is compared. Sections 4-5 (population floor P(p<1/2), plug-in vs LCB calibration miss probabilities) are a modest, correct extension a researcher could reuse; results 1-3 are textbook. Not new as framed, sound as mathematics.
evidence.domain: A sequential-analysis statistician would accept the algebra (verified exactly) and say results 1-3 are the OC/ASN curves; robust SPRT design for an unknown nuisance parameter is usually done by designing at the least-favourable p (which section 3 rediscovers) or with a mixture/GLR test, neither named. An HRI practitioner would note that goal inference in practice uses Boltzmann-rational trajectory likelihoods with a rationality coefficient beta that is inferred, not binary i.i.d. cues with known accuracy, and that 'the twin' here is a single scalar p_s; the paper states these limits but does not connect to the beta-inference literature. The calibration analysis (exact over Binomial(n,p)) is a good, honest touch.

defects.what: Results 1-3 are Wald's operating-characteristic and ASN functions of the symmetric binomial SPRT evaluated off the design parameter; the whitepaper presents 'the exact real-human consequences of tuning it in a twin' as the contribution without naming OC/ASN, and cites none of the HRI human-rationality misspecification work (Fisac et al. RSS 2018, which infers rationality online and is this paper's own 'next step'; Milli & Dragan UAI 2019; Bobu et al. HRI 2020), nor compares to an online or mixture-over-p baseline

The section-5 calibration code behind a headline README claim (miss probability 0.38/0.42/0.33/0.30/0.14) is effectively untested: changing the Laplace estimator, the miss criterion (e>alpha -> e>2alpha) or the p_hat<=1/2 fallback leaves all 6 tests green; test_demo_design asserts only pbad>0 and an ordering, and no test pins results.txt
Rounding slips in headline claims: 'doubles the error' is 2.2-2.7x; 'cuts that to <= 4%' but n=50 gives 4.02%
alpha^theta law stated as '2-3x off'; the quoted p_s=0.9 row is 1.7-3.3x off (and 12x at p_s=0.7, p=0.95)

design_h is an uncapped linear search (11.5M iterations at p_s=0.5000001) with a 10**6 sentinel for p_s<=1/2, although the closed form ceil(ln((1-a)/a)/ln r) exists; phat_design computes it in full before capping
Dead assignment `ps, w = None, None`, and the column labelled P(p<.5) is a proxy beta_pop_err(h=4000) rather than the Beta CDF
README and whitepaper carry no AI-assistance note (the served page does)

verdict: Correct and reproducible: every headline number (gambler's-ruin error and time, twin designs, population floor and error, calibration miss probabilities) was recomputed independently by an exact Markov-chain solve, the exact Beta CDF, an independent Beta Monte Carlo and a math.comb enumeration, and all match results.txt to the printed digits; run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte. It misses the bar on verification: 4 of 8 seeded mutations survive, all in the calibration code behind the README's section-5 claim. As research it is sound but mostly textbook: results 1-3 are Wald's OC/ASN functions off-design, and the HRI literature on inferring human rationality (Fisac et al. 2018 and successors) is neither cited nor used as a baseline. Claims are honest about limits, with small rounding slips. Scores 4/3/2/3/3/2/2, median 3; does not meet the bar (verification 2).
